title: Argument Completeness
description: Essential Criteria: Each argument contains all three components -- a clear claim, a warrant explaining why the claim is true, and an impact explaining why it matters to the resolution.

title: Resolution Linkage
description: Essential Criteria: Every argument is explicitly connected back to the resolution, not just to a general principle or related topic.

title: Evidence Quality
description: Important Criteria: Evidence is specific, attributable to an identifiable source or logical basis, and not presented as generic common knowledge when a more specific warrant is available.

title: Impact Framing
description: Important Criteria: The response frames at least one impact in terms that allow future comparison, like magnitude, probability, timeframe, or reversibility, rather than asserting impact without a measurable dimension.

title: Internal Consistency
description: Important Criteria: Arguments within the same turn do not contradict each other in their assumptions, values, or factual claims.

title: Missing Warrant
description: Pitfall Criteria: Does not present claims where the logical connection between evidence and conclusion is missing or requires the reader to supply the reasoning.

title: Unlinked Impact
description: Pitfall Criteria: Does not assert that an impact is large or important without providing any basis for that magnitude claim.
